quotes.text: Policies exist on paper, they're reviewed annually, they're signed and filed, but they're never technically enforced. A policy that lives only in a document is not a control, it's a wish.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A sharp formulation of why document-based compliance fails.

quotes.text: RBAC governs the actor, policy governs the environment. One without the other leaves you exposed in ways you won't see until something breaks.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Distills the key architectural distinction between RBAC and Azure Policy.

quotes.text: The audit first principle is the rule here. Every policy that will eventually deny must start its life as an audit policy, not for a day, but for weeks.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete, actionable rule for rolling out policies without breaking production.

quotes.text: A guardrail is a system constraint. It prevents unsafe actions but lets everything else move forward without stopping.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the guardrails-not-gates model behind secure developer self-service.

quotes.text: Compliance as code is not a security budget line. It's a delivery velocity investment. Governance that runs automatically doesn't slow developers down.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes compliance automation as a business case leaders can act on.

takeaways: RBAC decides who can act while Azure Policy decides what may exist, and governance at scale needs both, layered with identity governance, resource locks and monitoring through a management group hierarchy.
Policies should roll out audit first, then modify or deploy-if-not-exists, then deny, ring by ring and managed as code in Git with pull requests and pipelines.

Group-based RBAC, PIM, managed identities, Key Vault with RBAC authorization and purge protection, golden paths and Entra ID Governance turn compliance into a continuous, self-enforcing system aligned with Zero Trust.
hook: Manual governance with PDFs, spreadsheets and change boards cannot keep pace with pipelines that deploy in minutes, so drift and over-privileged identities pile up unnoticed. This episode is for Azure architects and security engineers, and lays out a complete blueprint with Azure Policy, RBAC, PIM, managed identities, Key Vault and Entra ID Governance to make compliance automatic, auditable and developer friendly.
